O.
FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard ( Second Revision) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 15 February 1978, after the draft finalized by the Pest Control Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council and the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 This standard was first published in 1963 and was revised in 1973. The second revision is being issued to bring its requirements at par with the developments in-the industry and also to take care of the stipulations as laid by Central Insecticides Board ( CIB). An additional test method for malathion content has been recommended as prescribed in IS: 1832�1978*. 0.3 Malathion dusting powder formulations are used in the control of pests of agricultural, public health and veterinary importance. 0.4 Malathion dusting powder formulation is generally manufactured to contain 5 percent ( mlm ) of malathion. 0.5 In the preparation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of the Insecticides Act, 1968 and the Rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions 'imposed under these, wherever applicable. 0.6 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS: 2-1960t. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as: that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE
1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for malathion dusting powders.
�Specification for malathion, technical <first ,,.';siotl ). tRules for rounding off numerical values (rtviseJ).

(S I 2568 � 1978 2. REQ,UIREMENTS

2.1 De8criptioD - The material shall be in the form of a powder, It shan be free flowing and devoid of lumps. Malathion, technical used in its manufacture shall have been uniformly mixed in suitable fillers, such as talc or pyrophyillite. It shan be free from extraneous impurities or added modifying agents. The materia), when dusted from a hand rotary duster, shall issue freely without clogging or bridging.
2.1.1 Malathion, technical employed in the manufacture of dusting powder formulations shall conform to IS: 1832-1978*.

2.2 The material shall also comply with.the requirements given in Table 1.

2.3.1 The actual value of the malathion content in the formulations shall be calculated to the second decimal place and then rounded off to first decimal place before applying the tolerances as stipulated in 2.3.

3. PACKING AND MARKING 3.1 PacldDg - The material shall be packed according to IS: 8190 ( Pa rt I )-1976t.
3.2 Marldag - The containers shalJ bear legibly and indelibly the follow.. ing information and any other additional information as is necessary under the Insecticides Act and Rules: a) Name of the material; b) Name of the manufacturer;

c) Batch number; d) Date of manufacture;
e) Net mass of contents;

f) Nominal malathion content, percent (mlm)j and g) The cautionary notice as worded in the Insecticides Act and RUles.
3.2.1 When bags are used for packing this material,' the pictorial marking for C USE NO HOOKS, DO NOT PUNCTURE', as contained in IS: 1260 ( Part II )-1973t, shall be stencilled on the bags.
3~2.2 The product

may ~Iso be marked with Standard Mark.

3.2.3 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. 4. SAMPLING
4.1 Representative samples of the material shall be drawn as prescribed in the C Indian Standard methods for sampling of pesticides and their � formulations' (under preparation ).
NOTE - Till such time the standard under preparation i~ published, the matter shall be as agreed to between the concerned parties.

5. TESTS
5.1 Tests shall be carried out by the methods as specified in col 4 and 5 of Table I. 5.1.1 For malathion content test, start with a sample containing � 0'05 g of malathion taken in a beaker. Add 50 ml of cyclohexane and mix for 20 minutes using a magnetic stirrer. Filtr under reduced pressure and wash the insoluble residue on the filter paper with three IO-ml portions of cyclohexane retaining the filtrate and. washings. Transfer quantitatively to a lOO-ml volumetric flask. Make up to the mark with cyclohexane, and mix and then proceed with a 10 ml aliquot of this for the determination of malathion content by the method given in Appendix A of IS: 1832�1978�.
0'15

5.1.2 For high temperature stability test, start with 25 g of the material and place the bottle in the thermostat maintained at 90 � 2�C for 20 hours. At the end of the heating period, remove and allow the material to come to room temperature, A suitable portion of this, after treatment as given in 5.1.1, shall be taken for the determination of malathion content by the method given in Appendix A of IS: 1832-1978*. 5.2 Q,aaUty of RealeDt. - Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and distilled water (S', IS: 1070-1977t) shall be employed in tests.
NOTE -- C Pure chemicals' shall mean chemicals that do not contain impurities which affect the results of analysi�,
